newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel suspends Hamas extradition request.
newsitem.headline: Israel suspends Hamas extradition request.

text.p: Israel on Thursday suspended its request for the United States to hand over a leader of the militant Islamic movement Hamas.
Security sources said Israel feared the extradition of Mousa Mohammed Abu Marzook would spark a wave of attacks in Israel and harm its struggle against Islamic militant groups.

"The Israeli government has informed the United States that at this stage it wishes to suspend its request to extradite Hamas leader Moussa Abu Marzook to Israel," said a statement issued by Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's office.
It said Netanyahu and other cabinet ministers took the decision after consulting legal and security authorities.
"The decision was made on the basis of considerations relating to security and the prevention of terrorism," the statement said.

Israeli and American officials had sought to avoid extraditing Abu Marzook to Israel in the middle of the crisis in U.S.-sponsored Middle East peacemaking. Abu Marzook gave up his fight against extradition in January.

In 1995 Israel announced it had formally asked the United States to hand over Abu Marzook -- alleging he was responsible, as the head of Hamas's political arm, for attacks that killed scores of Israelis.

Israel did not contend that Abu Marzook personally committed any of the violent acts, but charged he was criminally liable because of his high-level role in allegedly directing, controlling and financially supporting Hamas's activities. Abu Marzook has denied involvement in any violence.
